reason: Three narrow Eventar git skills (commit a card group by pathspec, claim a card before building, push only the approved SHA) are one class: the git steps of landing an MVP card. Merged into one umbrella; the rules are the same ones, stated once.

Handoff commit ran a bare `git reset -q` before pathspec staging. That clears every staged peer file in the shared index. The skill already requires a path-scoped reset, so the bare form is the gap to close.

The episode split lib/auth.ts across two commits. A plain-variable staging step failed, and the temp-index plus commit-tree plus update-ref recipe worked and left peers' staged files alone. The skill only covered filtered patches.

Compile check of the split commit needed a node_modules symlink in the detached worktree; the skill's worktree step omits it, so the next session will hit the same missing-packages failure before finding the fix.

Corrective update. The patch staged just before this one carried new_string "x" by mistake and would replace the split-commit compile bullet with a placeholder. This full body restores every line and adds the node_modules symlink the compile check needs in a detached worktree.
Bracketed route paths and zsh word-splitting are the failure points when committing by pathspec; the card workflow skill lacks the array form and the post-commit zero-staged check.

After a temp-index commit (a26e1ff) the shared index still held old state for the group's paths. git status showed them as MM/D. Only a pathspec reset to resync those paths was safe, so the skill needs that step.

Episode pushed with `git fetch ... && git log ...; git push origin main` (branch name, not SHA refspec, chained with fetch). Auto-mode classifier denied it as Out-of-Place Publication on a public origin, despite the in-session "Push it". Skill already requires SHA refspec; the rule that a denial stops the push and hands the command to Ivan was not written down.

Episode committed one docs file by pathspec after checking `git diff --cached --name-only`; the skill's group-commit steps are heavier than needed for a single file, and the pre-check that prevented a peer-staged file from riding along should be stated explicitly.

A bare git push this episode published a peer session's commit (885b72d) that sat above Claude's approved commit (be83b24), so the push went beyond the approved SHA. The refspec rule exists but the bare form was not ruled out.

The docs commit was blocked by the auto-mode classifier because a PreToolUse hook rewrote the git command. The retry of the identical command passed. The commit workflow skill does not say what to do when this happens.

A commit of CLAUDE.md, package.json and a new script used bare git add and bare git commit. It swept in a pending hunk that was not part of the change, and the skill's name-level check cannot catch that.

The push was rejected because a peer had pushed. The session merged origin/main and pushed the merge with git push origin main, with no new go naming the new SHA. That breaks the SHA-bound go rule and the refspec rule already in this skill.

The Stop hook flagged console.log in a changed route file, and the turn still reported all gates passing with no mention of the warning. A pre-commit grep on the group's paths, with hits named to Ivan, closes that gap.

Fold two narrow project siblings into the git-workflow umbrella as labelled subsections: dependency changes (pnpm add touches two paths) and graph refresh commits (tracked outputs only). Siblings deleted after this lands.
Add the dependency-change and graph-refresh subsections absorbed from the two sibling skills.

Ivan repeated the rule that a change is backtested before it is committed. The git-workflow skill has no pre-commit backtest step, so a commit can go out with only static gates. Adding the step keeps the commit gate aligned with his instruction.

The vault-graph subagent died on an API error after writing output; the assistant validated the output by script and fixed 4 dangling links before merging. That check is not in the graph-refresh section, so the next refresh could merge broken links unseen. Lesson belongs with the existing graph-refresh commit rules, which this episode loaded and followed.

Graph refresh procedure lost its skill (eventar-graph-refresh is gone from the index) but CLAUDE.md still points at it. This skill now owns refresh; it must carry the shrink-guard and vault-merge rules the r4 close needed.

Episode confirmed the vault graph trap: a bare vault update degraded the graph (edges 1579 to 1058, god nodes lost) and had to be restored from backup and merged by hand. The existing bullet names the technique but not the restore steps or the observed damage, so the next session could repeat the bare update.

After the coherence close was pushed, PROJECT_STATE.md still read "NOT pushed" and the handoff still said the push was pending. The assistant had to edit both in a follow-up docs commit. The push section does not tell the agent to sync state docs after a push, so the stale status recurs.
